notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #6: Underground Exploration
notes.content:
[h2]One Map, Infinite Layers[/h2][p]In Stormbinders, you don’t switch between separate maps. The entire world, including both surface and underground areas, exists on one continuous map. That means everything works seamlessly: units, storms, seasonal changes, and terrain effects apply across every layer.[/p][p]This is made possible by our multilayering system, which lets us nest any number of levels within each other. You can have undergrounds below undergrounds, hidden chambers within ruins, or underwater tunnels beneath lava caverns. Each layer runs within the same map and can have its own biome, rules, or events.[/p][p]In practice? We can create any type of dungeon labyrinth, vertically.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfT40L3wh7g23BtULAEyAiNnn-YZLCKGRvAN4Dmyns3AQ9XE118eqaMOc-uDUA5YU94wy0Kt4JfxWWEzZgmjC9daerdF8ns-6bM9tbZ6hhxAT4MfgZKICu822H_jH4i_fXcJQMp0XYm_byyzsowteY?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfsQelKGWW9Eoysb-gq7xp-Vs_twZraPmPJCDIBIjy6DQaMnN-mM-rTHDrXu3PNuo_EdXoUl5nq7NZysN3RvBvWY3hqWC8OOFDRinbbWDfssxMI74Ph26fMQrambOR4FkqktSjMiKEghlQROYsLkJ0?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][/p][h2]Any biome, even below ground[/h2][p]Every layer can have a completely different biome. Want a frozen cave beneath a scorching desert? Or a ruined city below an enchanted forest? No problem. Each layer supports unique weather, movement rules, terrain appearance, and atmosphere.[/p][p]This means exploration is never predictable. Under every mountain, a different world might be waiting.[/p][h2]Tactical and narrative potential[/h2][p]The multilayering system isn’t just visual, it’s a gameplay and storytelling tool:[/p][list][*][p]Hidden factions or entire underground bases[/p][/*][*][p]Ancient ruins that require finding an entrance below the surface[/p][/*][*][p]Changing combat rules (e.g. storms don’t reach underground, but other effects do)[/p][/*][*][p]Seasonal and weather rules that behave differently depending on the layer[/p][/*][/list][p]Undergrounds in Stormbinders are a fully integrated part of the gameplay with their own depth and mechanics.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdlP9s8LGi_XX-8MV8cfus4_F3Q_mKnXSExrUksSKAK3lIx9dPRsP0Z0YtoefYVk0dz1aqy7PmNrQnDqTafQ8Fbp6d4jYXy9-59fCf_YEP5jIozJSRjqJ-i5AVx16H-19k9PP_rAEoM6gu-kP_qQQ?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfPA-HI1O_lkAS158NavgTg9Jz90TqMZ2C4MWdmTkTcO40slURsZOXjmw2vL8R7eZe1UtOJSsBbxMW-ExN7SDa13t11GurIJIlo8kQZ80_b6gbWdNdXOmXoX50J-wjGRYS1yl0rZxGF2bP8wVFGNLc?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeZZDwBqWSKUoeQ0KZ9J_MDPBxTQ7bcdjfQkagaqqPfzhlwjRTZSTvEHYSTP6jHz29cxXPOg3p69krPfZJgTsl6EGd3G9jWLbYlGTwRAdrMPxtAHhyfVGsM1hb4s0LVKlr9b9euVSCHlDhU1IqpC64?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][/p][h2]Stormbinding and layered weather[/h2][p]Yes, Stormbinding works across layers, but not all storms pass through all levels. 

This means certain magical conditions, buffs, and storm-dependent units may act very differently underground.[/p][p]It adds a whole new layer of planning: sometimes it’s better to retreat below ground when a Deadly Storm approaches.[/p][h2]Tools for campaign creators and modders[/h2][p]Thanks to this system:[/p][list][*][p]Designers can build complex, multi-level locations full of secret paths, teleporters, and mysteries[/p][/*][*][p]Campaigns can guide players through different layers – like “chapters” of the same world[/p][/*][*][p]Modders will be able to use multilayering to create unique and immersive worlds full of hidden stories[/p][/*][/list][p]If you’re wondering why we went through the trouble of making it this flexible… it’s simple: we wanted deserts and forests in the underground too. [/p][h2]Custom underground rules[/h2][p]Inspired by the classics, and going against today’s trend of oversimplification, our undergrounds are not just cosmetic layers.[/p][p]Each underground level can have its own set of gameplay rules that change how other systems behave:[/p][list][*][p]Different movement rules (e.g. tighter corridors, no flying allowed)[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced visibility and spell range[/p][/*][*][p]No weather effects – or alternate effects like soul echoes or earthquakes[/p][/*][*][p]Limited access to certain units or spells[/p][/*][*][p]Modified economy – different resources, nerfed buildings, or limited construction[/p][/*][/list][p]This makes underground exploration a strategic experience of its own. It’s not just a change of scenery – it’s a different way to play the game entirely.

[b]Wishlist Now[/b][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

tags.feature: This is made possible by our multilayering system, which lets us nest any number of levels within each other. You can have undergrounds below undergrounds, hidden chambers within ruins, or underwater tunnels beneath lava caverns. Each layer runs within the same map and can have its own biome, rules, or events.

Every layer can have a completely different biome. Want a frozen cave beneath a scorching desert? Or a ruined city below an enchanted forest? No problem. Each layer supports unique weather, movement rules, terrain appearance, and atmosphere.
The multilayering system isn’t just visual, it’s a gameplay and storytelling tool:
Hidden factions or entire underground bases
Ancient ruins that require finding an entrance below the surface
Changing combat rules (e.g. storms don’t reach underground, but other effects do)
Seasonal and weather rules that behave differently depending on the layer
Undergrounds in Stormbinders are a fully integrated part of the gameplay with their own depth and mechanics.
Yes, Stormbinding works across layers, but not all storms pass through all levels.
This means certain magical conditions, buffs, and storm-dependent units may act very differently underground.
It adds a whole new layer of planning: sometimes it’s better to retreat below ground when a Deadly Storm approaches.
Designers can build complex, multi-level locations full of secret paths, teleporters, and mysteries
Campaigns can guide players through different layers – like “chapters” of the same world
Modders will be able to use multilayering to create unique and immersive worlds full of hidden stories
If you’re wondering why we went through the trouble of making it this flexible… it’s simple: we wanted deserts and forests in the underground too.
Each underground level can have its own set of gameplay rules that change how other systems behave:
Different movement rules (e.g. tighter corridors, no flying allowed)
Reduced visibility and spell range
No weather effects – or alternate effects like soul echoes or earthquakes
Limited access to certain units or spells
Modified economy – different resources, nerfed buildings, or limited construction
This makes underground exploration a strategic experience of its own. It’s not just a change of scenery – it’s a different way to play the game entirely.

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #5: Hero Design
notes.content:
[h2]Hero Classes – Archetypes with a Twist
[/h2][p]When we started designing our class system, we asked ourselves a simple question:
[i]What if each class could evolve and change over time?[/i][/p][p]That’s how our branching class paths were born.[/p][p]For example, here’s the progression path for a [b]Warrior archetype[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Knight (Might)[/b] → evolves into → [b]Paladin (Might & Magic)[/b] [i]or[/i] [b]Duelist (Might & Might)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Paladin[/b] can become → [b]Inquisitor (Might & Magic & Magic)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Duelist[/b] can become → [b]Warlord (Might & Might & Might)[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]So a single warrior archetype in a given faction has 5 stages of progression.
Add the Mage archetype to that, and you end up with 10 unique class paths per faction.[/p][p]At any stage, you can [i]lock in[/i] your current class – preserving your chosen specialization and its unique stat growth, skill trees, and talent distribution.[/p][p]It might seem like a small detail – but when you multiply 2 archetypes per faction × 4 factions, you end up with [b]40 distinct hero classes[/b].
Each of them comes with:[/p][list][*][p]unique active and passive talents[/p][/*][*][p]different ways of rolling for key skills[/p][/*][*][p]separate stat growth curves[/p][/*][*][p]and a ton of micro differences that make each class feel distinct.[/p][/*][/list][p]Each level-up doesn’t just raise stats, it unlocks [b]new class paths[/b] and options that are exclusive to your chosen combination.

But don’t worry – if you prefer a straightforward experience, you can mostly ignore this complexity.
Yes, it [i]does[/i] have an impact – and yes, min-maxers will have a field day with their spreadsheets.
But if you just want to play and level up your hero, you’ll still feel stronger and more capable, without needing to dive into all the systems.[/p][p]Power players will find deep optimization.
Everyone else? A hero who just gets better with time.[/p][p]
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd6lINYRv-ifMs1_goJnukqupaPiMHQ99hH5VlMQmygviy6eb4LoWMm6eGJ_3fsri9aSR24YKJQfwmH-8Z9KgZDXQgdq1WGyPjy8xMQ0ZSvKf0xg1LT2Q0vdiatCH_qsJKaD4DTP3D4g-Cm9AvuMQ?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeSLFA2kOvv0xSHxvbeUdc83WQsBhRRQV2IbPhaexf_EnPKWwwXHx_HQGNjyTzhrFGyVaRnIwo6RSWUW_wD3hrvaq_NVmsHsLzSJ1t2uPbWXzVQ8d1oh8eud_DneXk2HEaybJjXS2KJ6Tr307kUW5c?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXctA9wv-G-5onF66V5aZRoXcrPNm5Bh_o-S4MurM_oHMX1E_G3H989601I0L6VGH0k6sqFyEm3UcglKoE7ktoQdHr0h4vQhM0Hh-RazI_OxvVe3ZyhoIuIpcEdgNGIeP9UKag2dASks-WyFZcIkp0w?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeoG9NaKo8TWSzQ2MJHFPeUfnHbTfk_djWyinnZ_iwQXQlMrYfWMrjeLv05iV5cxZ7XDYpr45AwavvDFuVP4WNOuuEx4bLiKV3pP4SPaRE2M9hnoXZyaJ_3mel0tp2yLBfx-x6hkX66435_49GAnw?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdmd0YpLUvHGsebxoizkED-z39ofD2IouY4vzMETenKZTgHowdN1dpsSp2BseKsfU969WiUHf_rqAOZX2cL9VtcFCXlG1cRuS5NLHfQfFa7jtaK2sqQa-GGc14Hg4o8hYJPg7DhIyvDF5OvI9H5Eqo?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe52pDCKqmE7uHH09CtU33V5x42CHDPir2Q9r5qsmtZTo7Rq9LDhGA1muz9mQeePr259giUZdJ_GDcnrHdanMKmnAWx5YhZ4BQY5KHg3Ps_VMZil8IJW3gNK6PARDc-F2m7_hOdggTkEI4t2XZAjBw?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][/p][h2]
Talent Trees – Three Layers of Personalization
[/h2][p]Classes are just the beginning. The real fun in hero development comes from talents.
And we won’t pretend we invented something new here. There are dozens of talent models out there, but the one that truly stuck with us was from Heroes of Might and Magic V.[/p][p]Yes, we’re talking about a [b]Mastery Talent System[/b], where every main skill unlocks secondary perks, and it’s up to the player to decide how to build the perfect setup.[/p][p]Each hero in [i]Stormbinders[/i] grows using three interconnected types of talents:[/p][list][*][p][b]Faction Talents[/b] – shared by all heroes from the same faction, supporting their unique philosophy (e.g. better necromancy for Immortus, stronger storm manipulation for Astrion)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Class Talents[/b] – core talents based on the hero’s role (mage, warrior, leader), which define their main combat approach[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hero Talents[/b] – unique to the individual hero; these often break the rules and open powerful combos
[i](think: teleport for 0 mana, fire spells boosted during storms, or free summoning perks)[/i][/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks to this structure, we ended up with [b]hundreds of possible builds[/b].[/p][p]This means:[/p][list][*][p]One [b]warrior[/b] from Immortus can play completely differently than a warrior from Empyrium[/p][/*][*][p]One [b]mage[/b] from Helion might focus on summoning demons, while another goes full fire explosion spam[/p][/*][*][p]And the mix of [b]faction + class + unique hero talents[/b] creates dozens of playstyles and synergies[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcOFKc-W8zlnSXoR2EF_bpN1lHY2L3TDeQGtmW9lhs33UjgyAlx895RGmlPxvWQo65QSjdk0XOurQ8dqUIc6DI6VFg3bYd50xyTY94zLDmebrYcGZxN1cSFjeBckIrELT449G1_VfNRP7dT47fVGA?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfYV-slTdXX1YvKLxCITSbEmp69JNWajAqfqhh-XV7QqM2XeMak6-oMkVA5iIV7rFkRjML42OSktzFPXjMFIS97XozmjCTP1sY9aPfSjTl9UNRZ7G_T6Twc03bnp6Tg4XshCPphuXkQXXOBNVwG40k?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd7zj8hSrze4fOtErz5cvthA9XBD0Sq1oBKDBfJt4IRJNKmcPUjG21iaC9l6MGmg3YdLDvNwpcphapOgHXeGHZRo2p-wcMrRAGOdkx1cWlsN99qm2n602u_WmPYTNs6HLl9mbn1cPDTi5hT_eTR61E?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcHfLDlcW3iZIcSBy_T2-IFmeM9qGvnhW0N9i4nqBeTrKZE3gEMXIgvCoJw5y69C4Q9MRyqHzyFk14ibzWs1mf4pa3PyNg9P6eqV2my_dmDFO3mQePT0MQHRI_3gHr8qcFXVpMKfUlPId5y27Kwxg?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][/p][h2]
RPG in Numbers – Details That Matter
[/h2][p]Talents are fun, but what do they actually [i]do[/i]?[/p][p]For some players, they’re just numbers, but for us they’re pure gameplay.[/p][p]Each class in [i]Stormbinders[/i] grows differently. Every time they level up, they gain [b]unique attribute points[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Mages[/b] gain more spell power and faster mana regeneration[/p][/*][*][p][b]Warriors[/b] get better leadership, durability, and initiative[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hybrids[/b] unlock special combinations and talents that mix both styles[/p][/*][/list][p]Sounds nerdy? [b]Good.[/b]
[i]Stormbinders[/i] is a game built to be mastered, for those who want to dig deep into stats and theorycrafting. But don’t worry, it’s completely optional.[/p][p]You can also play on instinct and still have a great time.
The numbers are there when you want them, but they never get in your way.[/p][h2]
Heroes and How They Look – Quantity over Decoration
[/h2][p]While developing [i]Stormbinders[/i], we asked ourselves:
[i]How should we approach the design of heroes?[/i][/p][p]Should we create a small number of super-polished characters, with high production values and unique visuals like the biggest AAA studios do? [/p][p]Or should we follow the spirit of classic games, where there are [b]many heroes[/b], maybe not all visually unique, but differentiated by starting talents and class archetypes?[/p][p]We chose the second path and we believe it fits [i]Stormbinders[/i] best.[/p][p]By focusing on [b]quantity and variety[/b], we can easily add new heroes in future updates, each with new combinations of talents, classes, and specializations. This gives us more flexibility and replayability.[/p][p]So yes, [b]some heroes share their visuals[/b].
But what really matters is [b]how they play[/b].[/p][p]Every hero has:[/p][list][*][p]Their own set of talent options[/p][/*][*][p]Their own growth path[/p][/*][*][p]Their own unique combination of faction and class powers[/p][/*][/list][p]And if we ever want to add 10, 20, or even 50 more heroes, we can.[/p][h2]
Our Vision for Stormbinders
[/h2][p]At this point, we hope you’re starting to see what this game is all about.

We want to bring back that [b]magical feeling[/b] we had growing up – and take it even further. With systems you’ve never seen before. With dynamic weather, RPG-like hero growth, and deep tactical options.[/p][p][i]Stormbinders[/i] is our love letter to the past, and a bold step into something new.

We hope you’ll enjoy discovering it as much as we’re enjoying creating it.
[/p][p][b]WISHLIST NOW[/b]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #2: Beyond the Classics
notes.content:
We know many of you grew up with games like Heroes of Might and Magic, Disciples, or Age of Wonders, just like us. But from the start, we knew we weren’t here to recreate what’s already been done.

We asked ourselves not, “How do we remake a classic?” but rather: “What’s next for turn-based strategy? What else can we add to this genre before it becomes stale?” 

And after many tests and ideas, we landed on something surprisingly simple: There’s never really been a strategy game with a dynamic weather system, one with changing weather, magical storms, and chaotic elements that can either be harnessed or feared.

That’s how Stormbinders was born. 

[h3]Stormbinding Features [/h3]
At the center of the game is our stormbinding system — a system means weather is not just decoration, but becomes part of gameplay. It changes the map, the missions, the experience; and therefore your strategy and your choices. 
[list]
[*] It’s not just about snow falling or dust rising
[*] It’s about how ice forms on rivers in winter and lets you cross them in new ways
[*] It’s about lightning storms that grow and might block movement on the map
[*] It’s about how spells behave differently depending on the season — stronger, weaker, or with unique new effects
[*] It’s about how a smart opponent can build their hero to use the weather — and win with a smaller army if you don’t plan around the storm
[/list]
Stormbinding adds atmosphere, but more importantly, it adds new tactical depth — easy to learn, hard to master. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/8890e2f486aace40baa76407dd75e2e469242972.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/1d7899b659ad7c4e26187afa1bc671c82dff779a.jpg[/img]
[h3]For the Players Who Love Outplaying Their Enemies[/h3]
If you're the kind of player who loves planning and optimization, Stormbinders has a lot for you.
[list]
[*] You can build armies that resist certain types of storms
[*] You can use terrain to your advantage. (Why not try freezing the lake during a water storm and sneak into the enemy castle?)
[*] You can learn and control weather patterns and build your entire strategy around them
[/list]
Behind every decision, there’s a system. Behind every result, there’s a number.
But if you prefer to play by instinct, that’s totally fine too. Stormbinders rewards smart choices but doesn’t punish casual play.
Each biome has its own rules, and every storm behaves differently depending on where it strikes. Of course, we’ve also packed the game with tons of talents, perks, upgrades, and gear sets, many of which cancel each other out and are fully customizable.

So yes, expect those crazy combos where, if done right, you can two-shot a stack of high-tier units.
Why? Because you stacked Buff A, Buff B, Buff C, wore Set D, and became an unstoppable Fire Mage… until Player B stormbinds a weather shift that nullifies all fire magic.

[i]Tough luck.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/3513a18d1d18fca97482445d31991a3289406e56.jpg[/img]
[h3]Customizations[/h3]
New Systems? Yes, but Only If You Want 
Not everyone wants to learn new systems. Some people just want a classic strategy game with a good map and fun combat. 
That’s fine. That’s why you can turn off various elements, choose “always winter” maps, or play in “classic mode” if that’s your style.
Everything is optional and customizable. We believe players should decide how deep they want to go  (Screw the Designers, they don’t know how YOU would like to play).  

[h3]Nostalgia Meets the Unexpected[/h3]
We took systems you already know and love and added something new that makes the game feel much more dynamic, even though it’s still firmly turn-based at its core. 
Yes, it’s still a strategy game. But sometimes, your biggest enemy isn’t another player… it’s the weather you didn’t plan for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/eb7247e2c069202da607dee95b481d964a3ff800.png[/img]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/
